claim.quote: Lower limits on the nucleon lifetime are set for a wide variety of proposed decay modes.

date.note: Publication date of the final IMB-3 analysis.

key_value_text.quote: 935 contained events were observed. The observed rate and characteristics are consistent with the expected backgrounds from atmospheric neutrinos.
key_value_text.value: 935 contained events in a 7.6 kton-year exposure, consistent with atmospheric-neutrino backgrounds; lower limits on the nucleon lifetime for a wide variety of decay modes

name: Search for nucleon decay using the IMB-3 detector
notes: The individual lifetime limits are in the paper's tables, which were not fetched, so no single key value is recorded. An earlier IMB paper, Phys. Rev. Lett. 61, 2522 (1988), gave 90% C.L. lower bounds of (0.6–46.0)×10³¹ yr for 23 decay channels; it is not cited here.

summary.plain: IMB never saw a proton decay. Its final analysis of 935 contained events found nothing beyond the expected atmospheric-neutrino background and set lower limits on the proton and neutron lifetimes for many ways they might decay.
summary.technical: IMB-3 (3.3 kton fiducial) 7.6 kton-year exposure, 935 contained events consistent with atmospheric-neutrino backgrounds; lower limits on the nucleon lifetime for a wide variety of decay modes.

title: Search for nucleon decay using the IMB-3 detector
why_it_matters: APS News says IMB "quickly ruled out the Georgi-Glashow model and several other proton decay lifetimes".
